paragraphs.sourceText: Almost every child, on the first day he sets foot in a school building, is smarter, more 26 , less afraid of what he doesn’t know, better at finding and 27 , more confident, resourceful（机敏的）,persistent and 28 than he will ever be again in his schooling—or, unless he is very unusual and very lucky, for the rest of his life. Already, by paying close attention to and 29 the world and people around him, and without any school-type formal instruction, he has done a task far more difficult, complicated and 30 than anything he will be asked to do in school, or than any of his teachers has done for years. He has solved the 31 of language. He has discovered it—babies don’t even know that language exists—and he has found out how it works and learnt to use it 32 . He has done it by exploring, by experimenting, by developing his own model of the grammar of language, by 33 and seeing whether it works by gradually changing it and 34 it until it does work. And while he has been doing this, he has been learning other things as well, including many of the 35 that the schools think only they can teach him, and many that are more complicated than the ones they do try to teach him.
paragraphs.translationZh: 几乎每个孩子，在踏入学校大楼的第一天，都会变得比他在学校教育中的任何时候都更聪明、更好奇、更少害怕他不知道的东西、更善于发现和解决问题、更自信、足智多谋、坚持不懈和独立——或者，除非他非常不寻常和非常幸运，在他的余生中。通过密切关注世界和周围的人并与之互动，在没有任何学校类型的正式指导的情况下，他已经完成了一项比他在学校被要求做的任何事情或他的任何老师多年来所做的任务都要困难、复杂和抽象的任务。他解开了语言之谜。他发现了这一点——婴儿甚至不知道语言的存在——而且他发现了它的工作原理并学会了正确地使用它。他通过探索、实验、开发自己的语言语法模型、尝试并看看它是否有效、逐步改变它和完善它直到它起作用来做到这一点。在他这样做的同时，他也一直在学习其他东西，包括学校认为只有他们才能教他的许多概念，以及许多比他们试图教他的概念更复杂的概念。

paragraphs.sourceText: The fact is, the world has been finding less oil than it has been using for more than twenty years now. Not only has demand been 36 , but the oil we have been finding is coming from places that are 37 to reach. At the same time, more of this newly 38 oil is of the type that requires a greater investment to 39 . And because demand for this precious resource will grow, according to some, by over 40 percent by 2025, fueling the world’s economic 40 will take a lot more energy from every possible source.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，全世界发现的石油数量比二十多年来使用的石油数量还要少。不仅需求猛增，而且我们发现的石油也来自难以到达的地方。同时，这些新发现的石油中有更多是需要更大投资来提炼的类型。据一些人称，由于对这种宝贵资源的需求到 2025 年将增长 40% 以上，因此推动世界经济增长将需要从各种可能的来源获取更多的能源。

paragraphs.sourceText: The energy industry needs to get more from existing fields while continuing to search for new 41 . Automakers must continue to improve fuel efficiency and perfect hybrid (混合动力的）vehicles. Technological improvements are needed so that wind, solar and hydrogen can be more 42 parts of the energy equation. Governments need to formulate energy policies that promote 43 and environmentally sound development. Consumers must be willing to pay for some of these solutions, while practicing conservation efforts of their own.
paragraphs.translationZh: 能源行业需要从现有油田获得更多资源，同时继续寻找新的储量。汽车制造商必须继续提高燃油效率并完善混合动力汽车。需要进行技术改进，使风能、太阳能和氢能成为能源方程式中更可行的部分。政府需要制定促进经济和环境友好发展的能源政策。消费者必须愿意为其中一些解决方案付费，同时实践自己的节能努力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Inaction is not an 44 . So let’s work together to balance this equation. We are taking some of the 45 needed to get started, but we need your help to go the rest of the way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无所作为不是一种选择。因此，让我们共同努力平衡这个方程。我们正在采取一些开始所需的步骤，但我们需要您的帮助才能完成剩下的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions：In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. I Cry, Therefore I Am
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题纸 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。我哭，故我在

paragraphs.sourceText: A) In 2008, at a German zoo, a gorilla(大猩猩）named Gana gave birth to a male infant, who died after three months. Photographs of Gana, looking stricken and inconsolable (伤心欲绝的）, attracted crowds to the zoo. Sad as the scene was, the humans, not Gana, were the only ones crying. The notion that animals can weep has no scientific basis. Years of observations by biologists Dian Fossey, who observed gorillas, and Jane Goodall, who worked with chimpanzees(黑猩猩), could not prove that animals cry tears from emotion.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 2008年，德国一家动物园里，一只名叫加纳的大猩猩生下了一个男婴，三个月后就夭折了。加纳伤心欲绝的照片吸引了很多人来到动物园。尽管场面很悲伤，但哭泣的却是人类，而不是加纳。动物会哭泣的说法没有科学依据。生物学家戴安·福西多年的观察，他观察到大猩猩和研究黑猩猩的简·古道尔都无法证明动物会因情绪而流泪。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) It’s true that many animals shed tears, especially in response to pain. Tears protect the eye by keeping it moist. But crying as an expression of feeling is unique to humans and has played an essential role in human evolution and the development of human cultures.
paragraphs.translationZh: B）确实，许多动物都会流泪，尤其是在疼痛时。眼泪通过保持眼睛湿润来保护眼睛。但哭泣作为一种情感表达是人类独有的，在人类进化和人类文化发展中发挥着至关重要的作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Within two days an infant can imitate sad and happy faces. If an infant does not cry out, it is unlikely to get the attention it needs to survive. Around 3-4 months, the relationship between the human infant and its environment takes on a more organized communicative role, and tearful crying begins to serve interpersonal purposes: the search for comfort and pacification (抚慰). As we get older, crying becomes a tool of social interaction: grief and joy, shame and pride, fear and manipulation.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 两天之内，婴儿就可以模仿悲伤和快乐的面孔。如果婴儿不哭闹，他就不太可能得到生存所需的关注。大约 3-4 个月大时，人类婴儿与其环境之间的关系呈现出更有组织性的沟通作用，流泪开始服务于人际交往的目的：寻求安慰和安抚。随着年龄的增长，哭泣成为社交互动的工具：悲伤和快乐、羞耻和骄傲、恐惧和操纵。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Tears are as universal as laughter, and grief is more complex than joy. But although we all cry, we do so in different ways. Women cry more frequently and intensely than men, especially when exposed to emotional events. Like crying, depression is, around the world, more commonly seen in women than in men. One explanation might be that women, who despite decades of social advances still suffer from economic inequality, discrimination (歧视) and even violence, might have more to cry about. Men not only cry for shorter periods than women, but they also are less inclined to explain their tears, usually shed them more quietly, and tend more frequently to apologize when they cry openly. Men, like women, report crying at the death of a loved one and in response to a moving religious experience. They are more likely than women to cry when their core identities—as providers and protectors, as fathers and fighters—are questioned.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 眼泪和笑声一样普遍，悲伤比快乐更复杂。尽管我们都会哭泣，但我们哭的方式却不同。女性比男性更频繁、更强烈地哭泣，尤其是在经历情绪事件时。就像哭泣一样，在世界各地，抑郁症在女性中比男性更常见。一种解释可能是，尽管社会取得了几十年的进步，但妇女仍然遭受着经济不平等、歧视（禁止）甚至暴力，她们可能有更多的理由哭泣。男性不仅比女性哭泣的时间短，而且他们也不太愿意解释自己的眼泪，通常更安静地流泪，并且在公开哭泣时更频繁地道歉。男人和女人一样，都会因亲人的去世和感人的宗教经历而哭泣。当她们的核心身份——作为养育者和保护者、作为父亲和战士——受到质疑时，她们比女性更有可能哭泣。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) People who score on personality tests as more sympathetic cry more than those who are more rigid or have more self-control. Frequency of crying varies widely: some shed tears at any novel or movie, others only a handful of times in their lives. Crying in response to stress and conflict in the home, or after emotional trauma (创伤), lasts much longer than tears induced by everyday sadness—which in turn last longer than tears of delight and joy.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 在性格测试中得分为更有同情心的人比那些更严格或更自控的人哭得更多。哭泣的频率差异很大：有些人在任何小说或电影中流泪，而另一些人一生中只流过几次泪。因家庭压力和冲突或情感创伤（创伤）而哭泣的时间比日常悲伤引起的眼泪持续时间长得多，而日常悲伤引起的眼泪又比喜悦和喜悦的眼泪持续时间长。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Sadness is our primary association with crying, but the fact is that people report feeling happier after crying. Surveys estimate that 85% of women and 73% of men report feeling better after shedding tears. Surprisingly, crying is more commonly associated with minor forms of depression than with major depression involving suicidal thoughts.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 悲伤是我们与哭泣的主要联系，但事实是人们报告在哭泣后感觉更快乐。调查估计，85% 的女性和 73% 的男性表示流泪后感觉好多了。令人惊讶的是，与涉及自杀念头的重度抑郁症相比，哭泣更常与轻度抑郁症相关。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) People widely report that crying relieves tension, restores emotional balance and provides “catharsis,” a washing out of bad feelings. The term “catharsis” has religious implications of removing evil and sin; it’s no surprise that religious ceremonies are, around the world, one of the main settings for the release of tears.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 人们普遍认为哭泣可以缓解紧张、恢复情绪平衡并提供“宣泄”，即洗去不良情绪。 “宣泄”一词具有消除邪恶和罪恶的宗教含义；毫不奇怪，世界各地的宗教仪式是释放眼泪的主要场所之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Crying is a nearly universal sign of grief, though some mourners report that, despite genuine sorrow, they cannot shed tears—sometimes even for years after their loved one has gone. Unlike today, when the privacy of grief is more respected, the public or ceremonial shedding of tears, at the graveside of a spouse or the funeral of a king or queen, was once considered socially or even politically essential.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 哭泣几乎是悲伤的普遍表现，尽管一些哀悼者报告说，尽管他们真诚地悲伤，但他们却无法流泪——有时甚至在亲人去世多年后也无法流泪。与今天不同的是，当悲伤的隐私受到更多尊重时，在配偶的墓地或国王或王后的葬礼上公开或仪式性地流泪曾经被认为具有社会甚至政治意义。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Crying has also served other social purposes. Rousseau wrote in his Confessions that while he considered tears the most powerful expression of love, he also just liked to cry over nothing.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 哭泣还具有其他社会目的。卢梭在《忏悔录》中写道，虽然他认为眼泪是爱最有力的表达方式，但他也只是喜欢无缘无故地哭泣。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The association of tears with art has ancient roots. The classic Greek tragedies of the fifth century B. C. were primarily celebrations of gods. Tragedies, like poetry and music, were staged religious events. Even then it was recognized that crying in response to drama brought pleasure.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 眼泪与艺术的联系有着古老的根源。公元前五世纪的经典希腊悲剧主要是对神的庆祝。悲剧与诗歌和音乐一样，都是上演的宗教活动。即使在那时，人们也认识到，因戏剧而哭泣会带来快乐。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) I have argued that there are neurobiological(神经生物方面的）associations linking the arts and mood disorders. When I lecture on crying, I ask my audience to let me know, by a show of hands, which art forms most move them to tears. About 80% say music, followed closely by novels (74% ), but then the figures fall sharply, to 43% , for poetry, and 10 -22% for paintings, sculpture and architecture.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 我认为艺术和情绪障碍之间存在神经生物学联系。当我讲授哭泣时，我要求听众举手告诉我哪种艺术形式最能让他们流泪。大约 80% 的人说音乐，紧随其后的是小说 (74%)，但随后数字急剧下降，诗歌为 43%，绘画、雕塑和建筑为 10 -22%。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) The physical act of crying is mainly one of breathing in air, which is why we choke up when we weep. This suggests to language scientists that emotional crying evolved before language, perhaps explaining why tears communicate states of mind and feelings that are often so difficult to express in words. Of course, from an evolutionary perspective, recognition of emotion (usually through facial gesture) was essential for survival.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 哭泣的身体行为主要是呼吸空气，这就是为什么我们哭泣时会哽咽。这向语言科学家表明，情感哭泣是在语言之前出现的，这或许可以解释为什么眼泪能传达难以用语言表达的精神状态和感受。当然，从进化的角度来看，识别情绪（通常通过面部表情）对于生存至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) The earliest humans arrived several million years ago, but only 150,000 to 200,000 years ago, did cultures, language, religion and the arts arise. Along the way, tears became more than a biological necessity to lubricate（润滑）the eye and developed into a sign of intense emotion and a signal of social bonding. The development of self-consciousness and the notion of individual identity, or ego; storytelling about the origins of the world, the creation of humanity and life after death; and the ability to feel others, sadness—all were critical parts of the neurobiological changes that made us human.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 最早的人类在几百万年前到达，但只有 15 万到 20 万年前，文化、语言、宗教和艺术才出现。一路走来，眼泪不再是润滑眼睛的生理需要，而是发展成为强烈情感的标志和社会联系的信号。自我意识和个人身份或自我概念的发展；讲述世界的起源、人类的创造和死后生命的故事；感受他人的能力、悲伤——所有这些都是使我们成为人类的神经生物学变化的关键部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) More recently, we’ve learned from neuroscience that certain brain circuits（回路）are activated(激活), rapidly and unconsciously, when we see another in emotional distress. In short, our brain evolved circuits to allow us to experience sympathy, which in turn made civilization, and an ethics based on sympathy, possible. So the next time you reach a tissue box, or sob on a Mend’s shoulder, or shed tears at the movies, stop and reflect on why we cry and what it means to cry. Because ultimately, while we love to cry, we also cry to love.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 最近，我们从神经科学中了解到，当我们看到另一个人处于情绪困扰时，某些大脑回路会被快速且无意识地激活（激活）。简而言之，我们的大脑进化出了让我们能够体验同情心的回路，这反过来又使文明和基于同情心的道德成为可能。所以，下次当你伸手去拿纸巾盒，或者靠在门德的肩膀上哭泣，或者在电影中流泪时，停下来思考一下我们为什么哭泣以及哭泣意味着什么。因为归根结底，虽然我们喜欢哭泣，但我们也为爱而哭泣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Nowadays people respect the privacy of grief more than in the past.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 如今人们比过去更加尊重悲伤的隐私。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Infants cry to attract attention for survival.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 婴儿为了生存而哭泣是为了引起注意。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. There is no scientific evidence as yet that animals can shed tears from emotion.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 目前还没有科学证据表明动物会因情绪而流泪。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Tears can perform certain communicative functions which words cannot.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 眼泪可以发挥言语所不能达到的某些交流功能。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Our ability to experience sympathy is essential to the development of civilization.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50.我们体验同情的能力对于文明的发展至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. People are more inclined to cry when suffering minor forms of depression.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51.人们在患有轻微抑郁症时更容易哭泣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Sometimes people cannot cry despite genuine grief.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 有时，尽管真的悲伤，人们却无法哭泣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. In humans, long history, tears have developed an essential role in social relationships.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 在人类漫长的历史中，眼泪在社会关系中发挥着重要作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. Men are less likely to give reasons for their tears.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 男人不太可能说出自己流泪的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Crying has long been associated with art.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Hospitals, hoping to curb medical error, have invested heavily to put computers, smartphones and other devices into the hands of medical staff for instant access to patient data, drug information and case studies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 医院希望遏制医疗失误，投入巨资将电脑、智能手机和其他设备交到医务人员手中，以便即时访问患者数据、药物信息和案例研究。

paragraphs.sourceText: But like many cures, this solution has come with an unintended side effect: doctors and nurses can be focused on the screen and not the patient, even during moments of critical care. A poll showed that half of medical technicians had admitted texting during a procedure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但与许多治疗方法一样，这种解决方案也带来了意想不到的副作用：即使在重症监护期间，医生和护士也可能将注意力集中在屏幕上而不是患者身上。一项民意调查显示，一半的医疗技术人员承认在手术过程中发短信。

paragraphs.sourceText: This phenomenon has set off an intensifying discussion at hospitals and medical schools about a problem perhaps best described as “distracted doctoring.” In response, some hospitals have begun limiting the use of electronic devices in critical settings, while schools have started reminding medical students to focus on patients instead of devices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种现象在医院和医学院引发了一场激烈的讨论，讨论的问题也许最好被描述为“分心医疗”。作为回应，一些医院已经开始限制在关键环境中使用电子设备，而学校也开始提醒医学生关注患者而不是设备。

paragraphs.sourceText: “You justify carrying devices around the hospital to do medical records, but you can surf the Internet or do Facebook, and sometimes Facebook is more tempting,” said Dr. Peter Papadakos at the University of Rochester Medical Center.
paragraphs.translationZh: “你认为在医院周围携带设备来记录医疗记录是合理的，但你可以上网或使用 Facebook，有时 Facebook 更有吸引力，”罗切斯特大学医学中心的彼得·帕帕达科斯 (Peter Papadakos) 博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: “My gut feeling（本能的感觉）is lives are in danger,” said Dr. Papadakos. “We’re not educating people about the problem, and ifs getting worse.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “我的直觉是生命处于危险之中，”帕帕达科斯博士说。 “我们没有教育人们了解这个问题，也没有让人们了解这个问题是否会变得更糟。”

paragraphs.sourceText: A survey of 439 medical technicians found that 55 percent of technicians who monitor bypass machines acknowledged that they had talked on cellphones during heart surgery. Half said they had texted while in surgery. The study concluded, “ Such distractions have the potential to be disastrous.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项针对 439 名医疗技术人员的调查发现，55% 的监测搭桥机的技术人员承认他们在心脏手术期间曾用手机通话。一半人表示他们在手术期间发过短信。该研究的结论是：“这种干扰可能会带来灾难性的后果。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Medical professionals have always faced interruptions from cellphones, and multitasking is simply a fact of life for many medical jobs. What has changed, say doctors, especially younger ones, is that they face increasing pressure to interact with their devices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 医疗专业人员总是面临手机的干扰，而多任务处理是许多医疗工作的现实。医生，尤其是年轻医生说，发生的变化是他们面临着与设备互动越来越大的压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: The pressure stems from a mantra(信条）of modem medicine that patient care must be “data driven,” and informed by the latest, instantly accessible information. By many accounts, the technology has helped reduce medical error by providing instant access to patient data or prescription details.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种压力源于现代医学的信条，即患者护理必须是“数据驱动的”，并由最新的、可即时访问的信息提供信息。从许多方面来看，该技术通过提供对患者数据或处方详细信息的即时访问来帮助减少医疗错误。

paragraphs.sourceText: Dr. Peter Carmel, president of the American Medical Association, said technology “offers great potential in health c a r e , ” b u t he added that doctors, first priority should be with the patient.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国医学会主席彼得·卡梅尔博士表示，技术“在医疗保健领域提供了巨大的潜力”，但他补充说，医生的首要任务应该是患者。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: I have closely watched my generation, known as The Millennials, for 29 years now. Joel Stein wrote an extensive piece on
paragraphs.translationZh: 29 年来，我一直密切关注我们这一代人，即千禧一代。乔尔斯坦写了一篇长篇文章

paragraphs.sourceText: Millennials and he remains rather optimistic about our potential.
paragraphs.translationZh: 千禧一代和他对我们的潜力仍然相当乐观。

paragraphs.sourceText: I hesitate to share his optimism because of paradox (矛盾的现象）we seem to exhibit, namely, that there are more avenues for us to entertain ourselves than ever before, yet we are more bored than ever before.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我犹豫是否要分享他的乐观态度，因为我们似乎表现出一个悖论，即我们比以往任何时候都有更多的娱乐方式，但我们却比以往任何时候都更无聊。

paragraphs.sourceText: Entertainment has never been more varied. We have more cable channels, television shows, and movies than ever before. Internet providers allow instant viewing of almost any movie or television program ever created. Social drinking and partying are also widely available for Millennials. Every generation develops these habits at a certain age, but Millennials seem to be extending this phase of life as they postpone marriage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 娱乐活动从未如此丰富多彩。我们拥有比以往更多的有线频道、电视节目和电影。互联网提供商允许即时观看几乎所有创建的电影或电视节目。千禧一代也广泛参与社交饮酒和聚会。每一代人都会在某个年龄养成这些习惯，但千禧一代似乎因为推迟结婚而延长了这一阶段的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some of this is undoubtedly due to The Great Recession. Milleimials are having a difficult time finding jobs; only 47 percent of 16-to-24-year-olds are employed, the smallest share since government started recording data in 1948.
paragraphs.translationZh: 其中部分无疑是由于大衰退造成的。千禧一代很难找到工作； 16 至 24 岁的年轻人中只有 47% 有工作，这是自 1948 年政府开始记录数据以来的最低比例。

paragraphs.sourceText: But do Millennials respond to these economic troubles by doing whatever it takes to make ends meet? Hardly. In fact, of the four generations Pew Research has data for, the Milennial generation does not cite work ethic（勤奋工作）as distinctive of itself. Millennials want to save the world, but they sit and wait for that world-changing opportunity to be handed to them. Instead of working 2-3 jobs, launching a business, or doing what it takes to succeed, they retreat. Millennials may be the first generation to have a lower standard of living than their parents, but with this response to adversity(逆境), perhaps deservingly so.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但千禧一代是否会采取一切措施来维持收支平衡来应对这些经济困境呢？几乎没有。事实上，在皮尤研究中心有数据的四代人中，千禧一代并没有将工作道德视为其独特之处。千禧一代想要拯救世界，但他们坐着等待改变世界的机会交给他们。他们不再做两到三份工作，创办一家企业，或者做一切成功所需的事情，而是撤退。千禧一代可能是第一代生活水平低于父辈的人，但他们对逆境的反应也许是理所应当的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Much ink has been spilled in management books discussing how to get the most out of these youths in the workplace. Largely, they come to the same conclusion: Millennials are entitled, over-confident, and expect too much too quickly. We should not be surprised. Today’s young adults were raised by parents who made sure to boost their self-esteem at every turn, telling them they could achieve whatever they set their minds to, and handing out prizes for the sixth place.
paragraphs.translationZh: 管理书籍中大量论述如何在工作场所充分发挥这些年轻人的作用。很大程度上，他们得出了相同的结论：千禧一代有权利，过于自信，并且期望太多太快。我们不应该感到惊讶。今天的年轻人是由父母抚养长大的，他们确保在每一个环节都增强他们的自尊，告诉他们他们可以实现他们想要实现的任何目标，并为第六名颁发奖品。
